documents.title: Gynecology - Implant Removal
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward, DOB 10/16/1986   Seen 1/10/2025

Preconception visit and removal of etonogestrel implant (placed 9/2020). Implant removed intact from the left upper arm through a small incision under local anesthesia; steri-strips applied. No complications.

We reviewed early pregnancy care after her 2020 left tubal ectopic: positive home test should prompt a quantitative hCG and an ultrasound at 6-7 weeks to confirm location. Methadone to continue unchanged. Prenatal vitamin already started. She has an appointment with perinatal psychiatry next month.

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PERINATAL PSYCHIATRY CONSULTATION
Patient: Jill Woodward   Date: 2/20/2025
Referred by primary care for preconception planning.

Ms. Woodward is 38 and planning a second pregnancy. In November 2019, ten days after her first delivery, she developed an acute psychosis with insomnia, auditory hallucinations and a delusional belief about her infant, treated with a two-week admission and olanzapine; full remission, medication stopped 10/2020, no episodes since. No mood or psychotic episodes outside the postpartum period. Postpartum thyroiditis in the same period. Opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg for over ten years. Maternal aunt with bipolar I; mother with postpartum depression.

Mental status today: well-groomed, warm, euthymic, linear, no perceptual disturbance, excellent insight.

Discussion: Her risk of a recurrent postpartum psychosis after the next delivery is substantial - in the range of one in three or higher. Prophylactic lithium started immediately after delivery lowers that risk considerably; it would require level monitoring and planning around breastfeeding. Alternatives are an antipsychotic after delivery, or no medication with intensive monitoring. She and her husband asked good questions. She does not want to take lithium or restart olanzapine, and prefers a non-medication plan with close follow-up, understanding that medication would be started at the first warning sign.

Plan:
- No psychotropic medication in pregnancy or prophylactically after delivery, per her informed choice.
- Protected sleep after delivery: husband and her mother cover night feeds (pumped milk or formula), at least one 6-hour sleep block per night.
- Follow-up visit in the third trimester to finalize the written plan; early postpartum check-ins by video in weeks 1, 2 and 4, plus primary care.
- Warning signs reviewed with both: insomnia beyond one night, confusion, odd beliefs, hearing voices - same-day evaluation.

Perinatal Psychiatry

documents.title: Office Visit - Early Pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Positive HPT 3/25. LMP 2/21/25 -> 4w6d, EDD 11/28/25. Feels well, no nausea yet. No pain, no bleeding, no spotting. On prenatal vitamin. Methadone 60 mg (program informed). No migraines in the last few weeks.

Exam: vitals normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. Urine hCG positive.

A/P: Early pregnancy, location not yet confirmed. Prior L ectopic.
- OB referral sent urgently for early transvaginal US at ~6-7 wks; OB office will also follow serum hCG. Ectopic precautions reviewed again; she knows to go to the ED.
- TSH/free T4 today (history of postpartum thyroiditis).
- Perinatal psychiatry plan in place from February; will share our notes.
- Methadone - continue. Prenatal vitamin - continue. Acetaminophen first for headaches.

Re: Jill Woodward   Visit 4/17/2025

G3 P1 (1 term delivery, 1 ectopic). Transvaginal ultrasound today shows a single intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity, size consistent with 7 weeks 6 days by LMP; EDD 11/28/2025 confirmed. Adnexa unremarkable.

Prenatal labs drawn today are normal, including HIV and hepatitis C screening. Methadone 60 mg continues; we have contacted her program. Perinatal psychiatry plan noted and appreciated. Visits every four weeks.

documents.title: Headache in Pregnancy
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt ~17 weeks, usual migraine since this morning (L-sided, throbbing, nausea), like her typical ones. Took acetaminophen 1 g at 8, little help. No visual change other than light sensitivity, no swelling, last BP at OB normal.

PCP ok'd sumatriptan 50 mg x1 now, rest in dark room, fluids. Call back or go to L&D for any different/worst headache, vision changes, swelling. Pt agrees.
Callback 4:30: headache resolved after sumatriptan.

Re: Jill Woodward

Visit 9/23/2025 at 30 weeks 4 days. Pregnancy progressing normally; growth appropriate, fetal heart tones normal. Glucose screen normal. Thyroid tests this trimester normal. Tdap given today. Methadone 60 mg daily without withdrawal symptoms. Delivery plan includes a protected-sleep postpartum plan per perinatal psychiatry and newborn monitoring for methadone exposure.

documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Seen 10/21/2025 at 34 weeks. Euthymic, sleeping well, no psychotic symptoms. We reviewed the written postpartum plan with her and her husband: no prophylactic medication, by her choice, which she reaffirmed after we again discussed lithium; protected nighttime sleep from the first night (husband and mother covering night feeds); video check-ins at 1, 2 and 4 weeks postpartum; family knows the early warning signs and to call the same day. Copy of the plan to obstetrics and primary care.

OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received by fax)

Jill Woodward, DOB 10/16/1986
Admitted 11/28/2025 in spontaneous labor at 40w0d; discharged 12/01/2025.

Delivery: normal spontaneous vaginal delivery 11/28/2025, healthy infant. Labor uncomplicated. Placenta complete.
Postpartum: uncomplicated. Breastfeeding, with night feeds by family per the perinatal psychiatry plan; slept well each night in hospital. Mood stable. Methadone 60 mg continued. Newborn monitored per protocol and discharged with mother.

Discharge medications: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP), prenatal vitamin, acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed.
Follow-up: perinatal psychiatry video visit at 1 week; obstetrics at 6 weeks; primary care.

documents.title: Video Visit - Postpartum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, 6 days after delivery. Baby asleep on her chest.

Sleeping 6-7 hours a night - husband and mom doing nights with pumped milk, she nurses by day. Mood good, "tired in a normal way." No confusion, no odd thoughts, no voices; husband (on camera) agrees she seems herself. Saw perinatal psychiatry by video yesterday. Bleeding moderate and decreasing. Methadone 60 mg at the program, husband driving her. Breastfeeding well.

PHQ-9 3.

Exam: video only - alert, bright, coherent, appropriate.

A/P: postpartum day 6, doing well; history of postpartum psychosis - sleep plan working, no warning signs. Next psych video at 2 weeks. TSH at about 3 months postpartum (thyroiditis history). Call any hour if sleep slips.

events.reason: Right lower quadrant pain, 3 weeks postpartum

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: right lower quadrant pain and fever, three weeks postpartum, prior appendectomy. Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast. Findings: The residual appendiceal stump at the cecal base is thickened and hyperenhancing with surrounding fat stranding. Adjacent to it in the right lower quadrant is a 3.2 cm rim-enhancing fluid collection. Remainder of the bowel normal caliber without obstruction. Liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. Enlarged postpartum uterus. Ovaries unremarkable. No free air.
reports.conclusion: Stump appendicitis with an adjacent 3.2 cm right lower quadrant abscess. Postpartum uterus.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PHYSICIAN RECORD (received from regional hospital)
Date of service: 12/19/2025

CC: RLQ abdominal pain, 3 weeks postpartum

HPI: 39 y/o, three weeks after her second vaginal delivery (11/28). Pain began around the navel and over the past day has settled in the right lower quadrant. Low-grade fever at home, nausea, vomited once. Not eating much. No urinary symptoms, no abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding beyond expected lochia.
History: laparoscopic appendectomy 2018; laparoscopic left salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic 2020; postpartum psychosis after first delivery (remission, on a perinatal psychiatry monitoring plan); postpartum thyroiditis 2019-20; migraine; OUD in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg.
Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (dose confirmed with program), prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn, acetaminophen/ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Breastfeeding.

Exam: T 38.1 C (100.6 F), HR 102, BP 125/78. RLQ tenderness with rebound. Bowel sounds normal. Healed port-site scars.

Labs: WBC 14.0 K, Hgb 12.5, CRP 25 mg/L. UA normal.
CT A/P w/ contrast: inflamed appendiceal stump with adjacent 3.2 cm rim-enhancing RLQ collection.

Impression: stump appendicitis with abscess.
Plan: IV piperacillin-tazobactam, general surgery consult - for laparoscopy. Antibiotic choice and contrast are compatible with breastfeeding. Methadone continued. Husband bringing the baby for feeds; psychiatry plan noted to inpatient team.

reports.text: Specimen: appendiceal stump, completion appendectomy. Gross: short tubular segment with fibrinopurulent serosal exudate. Microscopic: transmural acute inflammation with mucosal ulceration and abscess formation in the periappendiceal tissue. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Appendiceal stump with acute appendicitis and periappendiceal abscess. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/19/2025 - Discharged 12/22/2025
Diagnosis: acute appendicitis of the residual appendiceal stump with periappendiceal abscess
Procedure 12/20/2025: laparoscopic completion appendectomy (excision of appendiceal stump), drainage of RLQ abscess and irrigation

Course: Started on IV piperacillin-tazobactam in the ED. At laparoscopy the residual stump at the cecal base was inflamed with a contained abscess beside it; abscess drained and irrigated, stump excised and the base closed securely. No drain left. Fever resolved within 24 hours; tolerating diet by POD 1; pain controlled with acetaminophen and ibuprofen, no additional opioids needed. Methadone 60 mg continued with confirmation from her program. She nursed in hospital with her husband bringing the baby. Inpatient team followed her perinatal psychiatry plan with uninterrupted night sleep; mood and thinking normal throughout.

Pathology: stump appendicitis with periappendiceal abscess, no malignancy.

Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily x 7 days (compatible with breastfeeding), acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed, methadone 60 mg daily (OTP), prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic 2 weeks; primary care within the week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call (completion appendectomy + abscess drainage, home 12/22). No fever since Sat. Taking Augmentin with food, no problems. Pain 2-3/10 on acetaminophen/ibuprofen. Eating, BM today. Sleeping at night - family doing night feeds, plan unchanged. Mood good. Visit with PCP 12/30 booked.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit with baby (4.5 weeks old) and husband.

Stump appendicitis with abscess, lap completion appendectomy and drainage 12/20, home 12/22. Discharge summary and path reviewed. Finished Augmentin yesterday. No fever. Pain mild, acetaminophen at night only. Eating normally, normal BMs. Lochia light.

Mood: good. Sleep 6+ hours on the night plan. No confusion, no unusual thoughts or perceptions; husband agrees. Psychiatry video visits on schedule. PHQ-9 2. Breastfeeding.

Methadone 60 mg via program.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Port sites healing, no erythema or drainage. Abdomen soft, no mass. Calm, bright, coherent.
CBC today.

A/P
1. Stump appendicitis with abscess, s/p completion appendectomy - resolved clinically. Surgery clinic 1/6.
2. Postpartum, history of postpartum psychosis - doing well at 4.5 weeks, plan working. Keep the night plan through at least week 6 per psychiatry.
3. History of postpartum thyroiditis - TSH late Feb.
4. OB postpartum visit 1/13 - wants implant again.

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry - Closing Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Final postpartum visit 3/10/2026, about 15 weeks after delivery. No recurrence of psychosis or mood episode. The protected-sleep plan was followed closely and is now being relaxed gradually; she is doing some night feeds without sleep loss. Discharged from perinatal psychiatry to primary care. Same warning signs apply during the first postpartum year and with any future pregnancy; she may self-refer back at any time.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Headaches came back after delivery - about 2-3 a month since February, same migraine pattern, no aura. Sumatriptan works; asked whether it's ok while nursing. Back at work since March.

Also: psych discharged her in March, no symptoms. Sleeping fine. Implant in. Methadone 60 mg via program.

Exam: BP normal. Neuro nonfocal. Weight down toward baseline.

A/P
Migraine without aura - back to her usual frequency. Sumatriptan is compatible with breastfeeding (very little reaches milk); no need to pump and discard. Acetaminophen ok too. Refilled.
History of postpartum psychosis - stayed well; closing letter reviewed.
Physical in September (TSH then).
